questions.q: Why is using `.getRowCount()` just to check "are there any matches" wasteful?
options: getRowCount() still requires the full query to run and find every matching row, even though only a yes/no answer was needed
getRowCount() always returns zero unless .next() is called first
getRowCount() is deprecated and throws an error
getRowCount() only works on the incident table
questions.explain: getRowCount() reports the count only after running the full query. Checking .next() once (optionally with setLimit(1)) lets the database stop early instead.

questions.q: What does `.setLimit(10)` do when added before `.query()`?
options: Caps the number of rows returned to 10, letting the database stop early instead of fetching everything
Deletes all but 10 matching records
Limits the query to run only once every 10 seconds
Has no effect unless orderBy() is also used
questions.explain: setLimit(n) caps the returned row count, which is useful when only a sample (like the 10 most recent records) is actually needed.

questions.q: Why is GlideAggregate faster than a GlideRecord loop for computing a COUNT?
options: GlideAggregate never retrieves full row data at all — it computes the aggregate directly
GlideAggregate doesn't support addQuery filters, so it always scans the whole table once
GlideAggregate is identical to GlideRecord but renamed
GlideAggregate caches results permanently after the first call
questions.explain: GlideAggregate is built specifically for COUNT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX and never pulls full row data, unlike looping a GlideRecord just to tally rows.

questions.q: What is the one-query fix for the N+1 company/incident example in this lesson?
options: Query incidents once with no per-company loop, then group counts in memory using the company field on each row
